title: EXP-129 — Create and Recover an Isolated FX_ Inventory Prototype Form
objective: Create exactly one new User-scoped Classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_InventoryPrototype01, using the existing verified basic-Form recipe. Set only its Form-level literal Caption to Inventory Prototype, perform one ordinary Designer Save, close the Form normally, reopen it through the supported recent-forms route, and verify that its identity, Caption and untouched baseline properties are recovered. Capture decisive before, after-Save and post-reopen evidence. The result is an isolated Form shell for subsequent separately authorized experiments, not a functional inventory dashboard.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md in full and review the relevant EXP-128, EXP-002-R2 and EXP-010 records before browser interaction.
Use the existing authenticated Mongoose session and verify live User editing scope.
Check that FX_InventoryPrototype01 does not already exist in the accessible Form inventory, with an appropriate positive-control check.
Create exactly one Classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_InventoryPrototype01 with Save Template unchecked.
Record the new Form's initial Name, Caption, ScopeType, ScopeName and comparison properties.
Set the Form-level Caption to the literal text Inventory Prototype.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after the Caption change.
Verify the saved Form is clean and the Caption equals Inventory Prototype.
Close the Form once using its Form-tab close control.
Reopen the same User-scoped Form once through the supported recent-forms route.
Compare its recovered identity, Caption and untouched baseline properties against the pre-close evidence.
Capture screenshots and concise observations under evidence/EXP-129/.
Create or update only the EXP-129 experiment record and its evidence files in the repository.
out_of_scope: Changes to existing MockLoginPortal, MockInventory, MockInventoryDashboard, MockLoginIDO or other Mock application artifacts.
Existing FX_CustomerPortal, FX_Orders, FX_Items and other unrelated FX_ artifacts.
Inventory data, authentication workflows, usernames, passwords and application records.
IDO definitions, SQL tables, IDO projects and collection bindings.
Form Scripts, global Scripts, event handlers and custom user controls.
Component placement, layout design, FlexLayout configuration and dashboard functionality.
Form/global-object unloading, cache experiments and metadata regeneration.
Cross-session persistence, database durability and backend serialization claims.
Modification or promotion of existing recipes.
Changes to EXP-128's historical evidence or acceptance record.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Do not modify any Mongoose artifact whose name does not begin with FX_.
Do not modify any existing FX_ artifact other than the newly authorized FX_InventoryPrototype01.
Do not proceed with Form creation if the exact target-name absence gate is inconclusive or fails.
Do not create a second Form or retry Finish after an ambiguous creation result without operator disposition.
Do not create or edit scripts, event handlers, IDOs, SQL tables, property classes or user controls.
Do not open or modify application records or credential-bearing data.
Do not perform deliberate reauthentication, logout or session replacement as an automatic recovery action.
Do not invoke Regenerate Form, global-object unload or cache-clearing operations.
Do not use direct internal database writes, unsupported APIs or hidden UI state as substitutes for the supported Designer workflow.
Do not perform additional Save, close or reopen cycles beyond the authorized sequence.
Do not change User Preferences or editing scope.
Do not modify AGENTS.md, environment settings, existing recipes or other experiment records.
Do not claim database durability, cache eviction or replay verification from an ordinary close/reopen.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence under evidence/EXP-129/ confirms a usable authenticated Designer, editing scope User, a clean initial state, and zero exact or case-insensitive matches for FX_InventoryPrototype01 in a functioning Form-name inventory check. A known-existing positive control must demonstrate that the filter works.

Creation evidence shows exactly one new Classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_InventoryPrototype01, with Save Template unchecked, the intended User-scoped identity and a clean initial Designer state. No second target is created.

Pre-edit and post-edit evidence identifies the exact Form and shows that only its Form-level literal Caption changed from its observed baseline to Inventory Prototype. Other comparison properties remain unchanged.

Exactly one ordinary Designer Save after the Caption change completes successfully. Captured response or visible product confirmation and a subsequent clean Designer state demonstrate the Save outcome; the Caption is read back exactly.
The target Form is closed exactly once through its Form-tab control, and evidence shows it is no longer open with no unresolved save prompt.

The Form is reopened exactly once through the supported recent-forms route. Post-reopen screenshots or captured UI state show Name FX_InventoryPrototype01, the same User-scoped version, literal Caption Inventory Prototype, all comparison properties unchanged and Designer Save disabled.

Final inventory evidence shows exactly one accessible matching FX_InventoryPrototype01 Form. The worker records the before-and-after target count, all authorized actions, errors, recovered values and limitations without claiming database-level durability.

The final evidence and repository audit identifies only the intended EXP-129 record and evidence changes, with no observed unrelated Mongoose mutations, preference changes, IDO actions, additional Saves, global-object unloads or credential exposure.

initial_instruction: PROPOSED EXP-129 — EXECUTE ONLY AFTER OPERATOR APPROVAL. Read AGENTS.md and the relevant experiment records in full. Establish a live User-scope Designer baseline and verify target-name absence through a functioning Form inventory with a positive control. If the target already exists, inventory evidence is ambiguous, scope is incorrect or the session is unusable, stop before mutation. Using recipes/forms/create-basic-form.md, create one Classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_InventoryPrototype01, Save Template unchecked. Capture its clean initial properties. Change only the Form-level Caption to the literal Inventory Prototype; capture the pre-Save value; perform one ordinary Designer Save; verify a clean Designer and exact Caption readback. Close the Form through its own tab control, then reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry. Capture the exact Name, ScopeType, ScopeName, Caption and unchanged comparison properties after reopen. Verify the final state and the single-target inventory count. Save all screenshots and concise evidence under evidence/EXP-129/ and record the outcome in the EXP-129 experiment record. No script, IDO, collection, component, runtime-record or non-FX_ application mutation is permitted. For a stale browser reference, allow at most one fresh snapshot and one corrected inspection before stopping with a blocker. Stop on any unexpected save prompt, identity mismatch, unexplained error rise or ambiguous creation result; do not widen scope or repeat potentially mutating actions. Classify any positive result as observed UI-level recovery unless a separate independent replay is later authorized.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261023-111214-OUiy. Rationale: EXP-128 established observational knowledge of the Mock Inventory application, including its Forms, IDO metadata and JavaScript integration, but modifying those non-factory artifacts is outside the learning factory's allowed mutation scope. EXP-002-R2 established a verified basic Form creation procedure, and EXP-010 established literal Form Caption recovery after an ordinary Save and close/reopen. The smallest useful next step is to establish one isolated FX_-prefixed Form shell for future inventory experiments. This reuses established procedures without introducing authentication logic, scripts, IDO changes, custom user controls or application data. It does not claim replay verification of a new capability.
